dedupe_keys.name: culvert v01 open source web application for culvert vulnerability to floods and flood induced erosion

description: CULVERT is an open-source web application that lets practitioners assess the vulnerability of road culverts to flooding, sedimentation and debris flow. It delineates watersheds from digital elevation models, estimates design flows with several hydrologic methods (non-stationary regional frequency analysis, the rational method and the graphical peak discharge method), and checks hydraulic capacity following Federal Highway Administration guidance for inlet and outlet control with Manning's roughness. Further modules analyse streambank erosion vulnerability, apply the Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation and model watershed debris flow, and the interface offers interactive maps, project management and automatic technical reports. It is generic and can be applied to culverts anywhere with suitable elevation and rainfall data. The application is publicly accessible online, the source code is on GitHub under the MIT licence and free, and a January 2026 Zenodo deposit holds example results computed from 10 m USGS 3DEP elevation models. Caveats: it is a first version by a single developer, the hydrologic methods follow US practice, and results depend on the elevation and rainfall inputs. It supports hazard exposure and climate adaptation screening of culverts and small road crossings, prioritising field inspections. It complements the FHWA hydraulic engineering guidance and is related to the RA2CE road network resilience toolkit.
